Finalize a STABL selection into a portable predictive model

Source: R/finalize.R
stabl_finalize.Rd

Takes a completed development result — a stabl_fit() object, or a stabl_analyze() result — and refits a downstream predictive engine on the selected panel using the full development data. The result is a "stabl_predictor" that can be saved with saveRDS() and applied to new data with predict() without carrying any training observations.

Usage

stabl_finalize(
  development_result,
  x,
  y,
  preprocessing = NULL,
  event_class = NULL,
  random_state = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'stabl_predictor'
predict(object, newdata, type = NULL, extra_columns = c("error", "drop"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'stabl_predictor'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

development_result

A "stabl_fit" from stabl_fit(), or a "stabl_analysis" from stabl_analyze(). For a validated analysis, the object must have been produced with final_refit = TRUE (the full-development refit supplies the selected panel); the cross-validated performance summary is carried into the predictor's development field, explicitly labelled as distinct from the full-data refit stored here. For an exploratory analysis the full-data fit is used and the development summary is labelled apparent / post-selection.

x

Development feature matrix (samples x features) with row and column names; the data on which the downstream engine and the preprocessing transform are fitted. Must contain every selected feature.

y

Development outcome aligned to the rows of x (named, or length nrow(x)). Factor with exactly two levels for family = "binomial", numeric for family = "gaussian". The family is taken from the fitted object, not re-declared.

preprocessing

Optional preprocessing specification: NULL (identity), a character vector of transforms for stabl_preprocess_fit() ("zv", "impute_median", "center", "scale"), or an unprepped recipes::recipe(). Fitted here on the full development data — the correct choice for a final model, since no held-out claim is derived from this fit. The stored transform is applied unchanged at predict time.

event_class

For binary outcomes, the level treated as the event for probability predictions; defaults to the second level of the outcome factor.

random_state

Seed for the downstream engine's internal cross-validation (glmnet path). NULL leaves the ambient stream; set it for a bitwise-reproducible final model.

object

A "stabl_predictor" from stabl_finalize().

newdata

Development-schema new data (see validate_newdata_schema()).

type

Prediction type: "response" (numeric; the only type for gaussian), "class" (hard class; binomial default) or "probability" (event probability for the stored event_class; binomial only).

extra_columns

Policy for unexpected columns; see validate_newdata_schema().

...

Ignored.

Value

A "stabl_predictor" object with the packed model, engine tag, family, outcome levels / event_class, selected_features, required_columns, the fitted preprocessing transform, the learner specification, feature_provenance (selection scores), a development summary, the stablr version and the call. No training observations are stored.

Details

The downstream engine mirrors the nested-CV machinery: an empty panel or degenerate outcome falls back to a deterministic intercept-only model (training event prevalence / majority class for classification, training mean for regression); a one-feature panel uses a glm (stored as bare coefficients); two or more features use a seeded glmnet::cv.glmnet() fit. Only binomial and gaussian fits are supported; other families fail clearly.

When preprocessing is NULL, new data must supply exactly the selected panel. When a transform is fitted, new data must supply all development columns, because the stored transform may depend on any of them; the panel is selected after transformation.

Functions

  • predict(stabl_predictor): Predict from a portable "stabl_predictor". The stored preprocessing transform is applied unchanged (imputation and normalization parameters are never recomputed from new data) and columns are matched by name, so input column order does not matter.

  • print(stabl_predictor): Print a concise summary of a "stabl_predictor"; invisibly returns x.

Examples

set.seed(2L)
ids <- paste0("s", 1:60)
x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 6), 60, 6,
            dimnames = list(ids, paste0("f", 1:6)))
y <- setNames(2 * x[, 1] - x[, 2] + rnorm(60), ids)

fit <- stabl_fit(x, y, lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.3, 0.2, 0.1)),
                 family = "gaussian", n_bootstraps = 20L, random_state = 2L)
final <- stabl_finalize(fit, x, y, preprocessing = c("center", "scale"),
                        random_state = 2L)
final
#> <stabl_predictor: gaussian >
#>   engine:      cvglmnet
#>   panel:       2 of 6 features
#>   selected:    f1, f2
#>   requires:    6 input column(s)
#>   preprocessing: center, scale
#>   development: stabl_fit (full-data refit; not cross-validated performance)
#>   stablr:      0.3.0
predict(final, x[1:3, ], type = "response")
#> [1]  0.1957291 -1.9545288  4.2163516
